overclaims: ITPro reported on October 15, 2026 that October 14 share-price declines extended to Oracle and CoreWeave. [e1]
checks.note: ITPro dates only the Dell, HPE and NetApp declines to 'yesterday' (Oct 14). It says the slide 'spread' to Oracle (-9%) and CoreWeave (-15%) without giving a date. Reuters (e2) shows CoreWeave's 15.1% fall ran from Monday's open to Thursday's close, so the rationale is wrong to date those declines to Oct 14. Minor: the proposition drops 'invariably' and says 'across the tech industry' where he wrote 'other companies in the tech space'. Outcome, axis and horizon match the agreed reviews.

overclaims: These records show investment growth in 2025 and a regional stock-market correction in October 2026; they establish neither a broad, sustained collapse across generative AI financing, investment and business activity nor that an eventual collapse cannot occur. [e1, e2]
checks.note: The public evidence quotes are cut to fragments ('growing more than\n200%', 'has lost 40%'). They leave out what grew (generative AI investment) and what fell (STAR50 index), so a reader can't tell what they refer to; the e1 quote also keeps a stray line break. The rationale calls a 40% fall that ran from the July peak through October a correction 'in October 2026', which gets the period wrong. Outcome, axis and horizon match the agreed reviews.

The public e1 quote is cut to 'scaling projects', which means nothing on its own. The evidence item's exact words are 'Many find that scaling projects outside of small environments or datasets can be quite tricky, said Rogers.' The e2 citation is correct. The rationale's figures and dates (Mar 20, 2025; 50.4% vs 35%; March 2026) match the evidence. The conditions, including the hedged 'could', are shown, and the outcome matches the agreed reviews.

The quote is exact. The price-rise condition comes from the surrounding passage and is shown in the payload. The rationale is supported: O'Reilly (June 9) on Copilot's June 1 usage-based billing, and Tom's Hardware (June 13) on firms switching to cheaper and open-source models. Limitations are worded carefully. Both citations are correct, and the open-horizon unresolved outcome matches the agreed reviews.
